title: The Linux CI jobs judge the test suite's time at twice the 60 s linux ceiling
goal: The GitHub kb-tests job and the GitLab kb-tests job set KB_TEST_TIMEOUT_FACTOR: "2" in their env, so tests.py's existing CI factor (tests.py seconds_factor) gives 120 s on Linux runners; _tools/tests_ceiling.json, its decision and the darwin 29 s ceiling stay as they are, and the local gate is unchanged. ST-moy5v7tm's measured p90 is checked against 120 s first: if p90 is above 85% of 120 s the item stops with a report instead of choosing another number. Evidence: reliability-authority-review.md CI-1 to CI-3.

run: import sys,re;a=open('.github/workflows/kb.yml').read();b=open('.gitlab-ci.yml').read();r=re.compile(r'KB_TEST_TIMEOUT_FACTOR:\s*"2"');sys.exit(0 if r.search(a) and r.search(b) else 1)

gates.question: Which policy do the Linux CI jobs use for the test suite's time (tests_ceiling.json and the darwin ceiling unchanged in every option)?
options: factor 2 on both Linux jobs (120 s)
time advisory on CI with its own exit code
gates.recommendation: factor 2 on both Linux jobs (120 s)
